name: Google Apigee
description: Protects against destructive Google Apigee CLI and apigeecli operations.

destructive_patterns.name: gcloud-apigee-apis-delete
destructive_patterns.description: gcloud apigee apis delete removes an API proxy from Apigee.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
Deleting an API proxy removes all its revisions and deployment history. Any \ applications relying on this API will immediately receive errors. API keys \ and quotas associated with products referencing this API may be affected.

\ Safer alternatives: \ - gcloud apigee apis list: Review APIs before deletion \ - gcloud apigee deployments undeploy: Undeploy first to verify impact \ - Export the API proxy bundle before deletion for backup

destructive_patterns.name: gcloud-apigee-environments-delete
destructive_patterns.description: gcloud apigee environments delete removes an Apigee environment.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
Deleting an environment removes all deployed API proxies, target servers, \ key-value maps, and caches within it. This is irreversible and will break \ all API traffic routed through this environment.

\ Safer alternatives: \ - gcloud apigee environments describe: Review environment contents \ - Undeploy all APIs from the environment first \ - Export environment configuration and resources before deletion

destructive_patterns.name: gcloud-apigee-developers-delete
destructive_patterns.description: gcloud apigee developers delete removes a developer from Apigee.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
Deleting a developer also deletes all their apps and associated API keys. \ Any applications using those keys will immediately lose API access. Developer \ analytics and usage history are also removed.

\ Safer alternatives: \ - gcloud apigee developers describe: Review developer details \ - Revoke individual app credentials instead of deleting the developer \ - Set developer status to inactive rather than deleting

destructive_patterns.name: gcloud-apigee-products-delete
destructive_patterns.description: gcloud apigee products delete removes an API product from Apigee.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
Deleting an API product immediately revokes access for all apps subscribed \ to it. Quota settings, rate limits, and access controls defined in the product \ are lost. Apps will need to be re-subscribed to a different product.

\ Safer alternatives: \ - gcloud apigee products describe: Review product configuration \ - Remove individual apps from the product instead \ - Set product access to private before deletion to verify impact

destructive_patterns.name: gcloud-apigee-organizations-delete
destructive_patterns.description: gcloud apigee organizations delete removes an entire Apigee organization.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
Deleting an organization permanently removes ALL environments, API proxies, \ products, developers, apps, and analytics data. This is irreversible and will \ completely destroy your API management infrastructure.

\ Safer alternatives: \ - Export all configurations and proxy bundles before deletion \ - Delete individual resources to verify nothing is still in use \ - Consider disabling billing instead if just reducing costs

destructive_patterns.name: gcloud-apigee-deployments-undeploy
destructive_patterns.description: gcloud apigee deployments undeploy removes an API deployment.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
Undeploying an API proxy stops all traffic processing for that API in the \ specified environment. Clients will receive errors until the API is redeployed. \ This is reversible by redeploying the proxy.

\ Safer alternatives: \ - gcloud apigee deployments list: Review current deployments \ - Test in a non-production environment first \ - Deploy a new revision instead of undeploying

destructive_patterns.name: apigeecli-apis-delete
destructive_patterns.description: apigeecli apis delete removes an API proxy from Apigee.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
Deleting an API proxy removes all its revisions and deployment history. Any \ applications relying on this API will immediately receive errors.

\ Safer alternatives: \ - apigeecli apis list: Review APIs before deletion \ - apigeecli apis export: Export the proxy bundle for backup \ - Undeploy from all environments first to verify impact

destructive_patterns.name: apigeecli-products-delete
destructive_patterns.description: apigeecli products delete removes an API product from Apigee.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
Deleting an API product immediately revokes access for all subscribed apps. \ Quota settings and rate limits are permanently lost.

\ Safer alternatives: \ - apigeecli products list: Review products before deletion \ - apigeecli products get: Check which apps are using the product \ - Remove apps from the product first to verify impact

destructive_patterns.name: apigeecli-developers-delete
destructive_patterns.description: apigeecli developers delete removes a developer from Apigee.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
Deleting a developer also deletes all their apps and API keys. Applications \ using those keys will immediately lose access.

\ Safer alternatives: \ - apigeecli developers list: Review developers before deletion \ - apigeecli apps list: Check developer's apps first \ - Set developer status to inactive instead of deleting

destructive_patterns.name: apigeecli-envs-delete
destructive_patterns.description: apigeecli envs delete removes an Apigee environment.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
Deleting an environment removes all deployed proxies, target servers, and \ configurations. This breaks all API traffic through that environment.

\ Safer alternatives: \ - apigeecli envs list: Review environments before deletion \ - Export all environment resources before deletion \ - Undeploy all APIs first to verify nothing is in use

destructive_patterns.name: apigeecli-orgs-delete
destructive_patterns.description: apigeecli orgs delete removes an entire Apigee organization.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
Deleting an organization permanently removes ALL resources: environments, \ APIs, products, developers, apps, and analytics. This is completely irreversible.

\ Safer alternatives: \ - Export all configurations before deletion \ - Delete individual resources first to verify impact \ - Contact support if you need to preserve any data

destructive_patterns.name: apigeecli-apps-delete
destructive_patterns.description: apigeecli apps delete removes a developer app from Apigee.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
Deleting an app revokes all its API keys and credentials. Any systems using \ those keys will immediately lose API access.

\ Safer alternatives: \ - apigeecli apps list: Review apps before deletion \ - Revoke individual credentials instead of deleting the app \ - Set app status to revoked to disable without deleting

destructive_patterns.name: apigeecli-keyvaluemaps-delete
destructive_patterns.description: apigeecli keyvaluemaps delete removes a key-value map from Apigee.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
Deleting a KVM removes all stored key-value pairs. API proxies reading from \ this KVM will fail or return errors. Configuration data stored in the KVM is \ permanently lost.

\ Safer alternatives: \ - apigeecli keyvaluemaps list: Review KVMs before deletion \ - Export KVM entries before deletion \ - Check which proxies reference this KVM first

destructive_patterns.name: apigeecli-targetservers-delete
destructive_patterns.description: apigeecli targetservers delete removes a target server from Apigee.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
Deleting a target server breaks all API proxies that route traffic to it. \ Requests will fail until proxies are updated to use a different target.

\ Safer alternatives: \ - apigeecli targetservers list: Review targets before deletion \ - Update API proxies to use a different target first \ - Set the target server to disabled to test impact
